entries.definition: FLUX, BLOODY, or dysentery, Acts 28:8.
entries.definition_ko: 이질을 뜻한다(사도행전 28:8).

entries.definition: FLY, the name of a large tribe of insects, some of which are exceedingly annoying and destructive, Isa 7:18. They abound in Egypt and Palestine. One species, which is found by modern travellers in the vicinity of the Nile, and called the Abyssinian fly, is as large as a bee, and is such an annoyance to cattle and other large animals as to oblige them to forsake their pastures and ranges, and to flee to some place where they can roll themselves in the mud or sand. Hence we may judge of the terrible nature of the judgments mentioned in Ex 8:24; Isa 7:18; in which last passage we are informed that the fly shall be found in the very places to which the cattle resort to rid themselves of its presence.
entries.definition_ko: 곤충의 큰 무리를 가리키는 이름으로, 그중 일부는 몹시 성가시고 파괴적이다(이사야 7:18). 애굽과 팔레스타인에 많다. 나일 근처에서 근래 여행자들이 발견한 아비시니아 파리라는 한 종은 벌만 하며, 가축과 큰 짐승을 어찌나 괴롭히는지 초장을 버리고 진흙이나 모래에 뒹굴 수 있는 곳으로 달아나게 만든다. 여기서 출애굽기 8:24과 이사야 7:18의 심판이 얼마나 끔찍한 것인지 짐작할 수 있다.

entries.definition: FOLD. See Sheep.
entries.definition_ko: 양 참조.

entries.definition: FOL'LY, Gen 34:7, FOOL, Prov 15:5. These terms are used by the sacred writers sometimes to denote weakness of understanding, Ps 14:1; 1 Cor 1:27; 1 Cor 4:10 and sometimes sin or wickedness. Ps 38:5; Josh 7:15. The transgression and disobedience of Adam were the height of folly, as is the sin of humanity generally. Foolish talking, jesting, foolish and unlearned questions, etc., 2 Tim 2:23, are such as are vain, frivolous, or have no useful tendency. The phrase "Thou fool," Matt 5:22, implies not only an angry temper, but probably also impiety and wickedness, in allusion to Ps 14:1, where the atheist is called a fool.
entries.definition_ko: 성경 기자들은 이 말들을 때로 이해력의 약함(시편 14:1, 고린도전서 1:27, 4:10), 때로 죄나 악함(시편 38:5, 여호수아 7:15)을 뜻하는 데 쓴다. 아담의 범죄와 불순종은 어리석음의 극치였고 인류의 죄가 대체로 그러하다. '어리석은 말'과 '희롱의 말', '어리석고 무식한 변론'(디모데후서 2:23) 등은 헛되고 경박하거나 유익이 없는 것을 뜻한다. '라가라 하는 자'(마태복음 5:22)라는 표현은 노한 성정뿐 아니라 아마도 불경건과 악함까지 함축하는데, 무신론자를 어리석은 자라 부르는 시편 14:1을 염두에 둔 것이다.

entries.definition: FOOD. Gen 3:6. We may form some judgment of the ancient diet from what we know of that of the modern Orientals. Vegetable food is much more common than animal. Instead of butter, lard, and suet, they use olive oil. A soup, or rather pottage, of beans and lentiles, seasoned with garlic and oil, is still, as it was of old, a favorite dish. The "red pottage of lentiles" for which Esau sold his birthright was something of this kind. Eggs, honey, milk (especially sour milk), and garden productions of every kind afford the principal materials of Eastern diet. The most common dish at this day in the East is the pilan, which consists of rice cooked with meat so as to make a sort of broth, seasoned variously and colored blue, red, or yellow. We do not find the use of animal food often occurring, except upon the occasion of entertainments, or the exhibition of hospitality to a friend, Gen 18:7; Luke 15:23, or upon the tables of the rich. The animals used for this purpose, especially neat cattle, were often "stalled" and "fattened." 1 Sam 16:20; 1 Sam 28:24; 1 Kgs 4:23; Neh 5:18; Isa 1:11; Isa 11:6; Jer 46:21; Eze 39:18; Am 6:4; Mal 4:2. Wild game, lambs, and kids constituted the favorite viands in the East. At this day beef is not much used, though from some texts above and other similar authorities we learn that the flesh of young bullocks and stall-fed oxen was highly prized. Prov 15:17; Matt 22:4. In very ancient times it was always the master of the house, whether he were rich or poor, who slew the animal. Jud 6:19. Grecian and Roman writers mention a like custom of later times. The preparation of the food by cooking was the business of the mistress. The shoulder was probably the choicest part. 1 Sam 9:24. It is customary for the Arabs to serve up at one meal the whole of any animal which they have killed. This is occasioned in some measure by the difficulty of preserving fresh meat in the Eastern climate. Gen 18:7:Luke 15:23. The people of the East are particularly fond of fish, and in Egypt this constitutes a very important part of their subsistence. Num 11:5. See Fish.
entries.definition_ko:
먹을거리. 창세기 3장 6절이다.

옛적의 먹을거리는 오늘 동방 사람의 것을 아는 데서 어느 정도 짐작할 수 있다. 식물성 먹을거리가 짐승의 것보다 훨씬 흔하다. 버터와 돼지기름과 쇠기름 대신 그들은 감람유를 쓴다.

콩과 팥으로 만들어 마늘과 기름으로 맛을 낸 국 곧 죽이 옛적과 마찬가지로 오늘도 즐겨 먹는 음식이다. 에서가 장자의 권리를 팔고 받은 「붉은 팥죽」이 이런 것이었다.

달걀과 꿀과 젖, 특히 시큼한 젖과 온갖 밭의 소출이 동방 먹을거리의 주된 재료를 이룬다.

오늘 동방에서 가장 흔한 음식은 필라프이니, 쌀을 고기와 함께 익혀 국물처럼 만든 것으로 여러 가지로 맛을 내고 파랗거나 붉거나 노랗게 물들인다.

짐승의 고기를 쓰는 일은 잔치를 베풀 때나 벗에게 손 대접을 할 때, 창세기 18장 7절과 누가복음 15장 23절이다, 또는 부유한 이의 상에서 말고는 자주 나오지 않는다.

이 목적에 쓰인 짐승, 특히 소는 흔히 「외양간에 매어」 「살지게」 하였다. 사무엘상 16장 20절과 사무엘상 28장 24절과 열왕기상 4장 23절과 느헤미야 5장 18절과 이사야 1장 11절과 이사야 11장 6절과 예레미야 46장 21절과 에스겔 39장 18절과 아모스 6장 4절과 말라기 4장 2절이다.

들짐승 고기와 어린양과 염소 새끼가 동방에서 즐겨 먹는 음식이었다. 오늘 쇠고기는 그리 많이 쓰이지 않으나, 위에 든 대목과 그 밖의 비슷한 자료에서 우리는 어린 수소와 외양간에서 살지게 한 소의 고기가 크게 값졌음을 안다. 잠언 15장 17절과 마태복음 22장 4절이다.

아주 옛적에는 부유하든 가난하든 언제나 그 집 주인이 짐승을 잡았다. 사사기 6장 19절이다. 헬라와 로마 저술가들이 뒤의 시대에 비슷한 관습이 있었음을 언급한다. 먹을거리를 익혀 마련하는 일은 안주인의 일이었다.

어깨가 아마도 가장 좋은 부위였을 것이다. 사무엘상 9장 24절이다.

아라비아 사람은 잡은 짐승 전부를 한 끼에 차려 내는 것이 관례다. 이는 얼마쯤 동방 기후에서 날고기를 보관하기 어렵기 때문이다. 창세기 18장 7절과 누가복음 15장 23절이다.

동방 사람은 물고기를 각별히 좋아하며, 애굽에서는 그것이 살아가는 데 매우 중요한 몫을 이룬다. 민수기 11장 5절이다.

「물고기」 항목 참조.

「※ 원문 결함: 영문 원문에서 창세기 18장 7절과 누가복음 15장 23절 사이에 쌍반점 자리에 쌍점이 찍히고 띄어쓰기도 빠져 있다. 디지털화 과정에서 생긴 흠이다.」

entries.definition: FOOT'MAN. The term sometimes means soldiers on foot or infantry. At other times it has special reference to the king's guard. 1 Sam 22:17. The word there translated "footman " is rendered "guard" in other passages. 1 Kgs 14:28; 2 Kgs 11:4, etc.
entries.definition_ko: 때로 걸어 다니는 군사, 곧 보병을 뜻한다. 다른 곳에서는 특히 왕의 호위병을 가리킨다(사무엘상 22:17). 거기서 '보행자'로 옮긴 말이 다른 구절에서는 '시위대'로 번역된다(열왕기상 14:28, 열왕기하 11:4).

entries.definition: FOOT'STOOL. 2 Chr 9:18. Kings and other rulers sitting in state required a stool upon which to rest their feet. The divine glory, which resided symbolically in the holy place between the cherubim above the ark, is supposed to use the ark as a footstool. 1 Chr 28:2; Ps 99:5. So the earth is called God's footstool by the same expressive figure which represents heaven as his throne.
entries.definition_ko: 왕과 통치자들이 정좌할 때 발을 얹는 받침이 필요했다(역대하 9:18). 궤 위 그룹 사이 성소에 상징적으로 머무는 신적 영광이 궤를 발등상으로 삼는 것으로 여겨진다(역대상 28:2, 시편 99:5). 하늘을 그 보좌로 나타내는 같은 표현으로 땅을 하나님의 발등상이라 부른다.

entries.definition: FOOT, WA'TERING WITH THE, a phrase used of Egypt in Deut 11:10, because the "Egyptians watered with the foot in two ways — by the tread-wheel working sets of pumps, and by means of artificial channels connected with reservoirs, and opened, turned, or closed by the feet." — Bible Commentary.
entries.definition_ko: 신명기 11:10에서 애굽에 대해 쓰인 표현이다. '애굽 사람이 두 가지 방식으로 발로 물을 댔으니, 발로 밟는 수차로 펌프를 돌리는 것과, 저수지에 이어진 인공 수로를 발로 열고 돌리고 막는 것이었다.'

entries.definition: FORD, a word frequently used to designate the crossing of any stream, but especially of the Jordan, as Josh 2:7; Jud 3:28; Jud 12:5-6; of the Jabbok, Gen 32:22; of the Arnon, Isa 16:2; of the Euphrates. Jer 51:32. Until recently the fords of the Jordan were supposed to be only 8 or 10 in number, but the British Palestine Survey has noted about 50.
entries.definition_ko: 어떤 시내든 건너는 곳을 가리키는 데 자주 쓰이나, 특히 요단(여호수아 2:7, 사사기 3:28, 12:5-6), 얍복(창세기 32:22), 아르논(이사야 16:2), 유브라데(예레미야 51:32)의 나루를 뜻한다. 최근까지 요단의 나루는 8~10곳뿐으로 여겨졌으나 영국 팔레스타인 조사단이 약 50곳을 확인했다.

entries.definition: FORE'HEAD. Inasmuch as modest women kept the forehead covered with a veil, not to do so was indicative of shamelessness. Jer 3:3. Jewels for the forehead, Eze 16:12, were nose jewels, although at the present day in the East women wear jewels and strings of coins across their foreheads. To mark the forehead with the device of a god denoted the consecration of the intellect unto it. Thus, the mark of the beast was upon the forehead. Rev 13:16. So God's name is upon the saint's forehead. Rev 22:4.
entries.definition_ko: 정숙한 여인은 이마를 너울로 가렸으므로 그렇게 하지 않는 것은 뻔뻔함의 표시였다(예레미야 3:3). 에스겔 16:12의 '이마의 보석'은 코걸이였으나, 오늘날 동방 여인들은 이마를 가로질러 보석과 동전 줄을 두른다. 이마에 신의 표를 새기는 것은 지성을 그에게 바침을 뜻했다. 그래서 짐승의 표가 이마에 있고(요한계시록 13:16) 하나님의 이름이 성도의 이마에 있다(요한계시록 22:4).

entries.definition: FOR'EIGNER, any one not of the genuine Hebrew stock. Ex 12:45; comp. Eph 2:12.
entries.definition_ko: 순수한 히브리 혈통이 아닌 모든 사람을 가리킨다(출애굽기 12:45, 에베소서 2:12).

entries.definition: FOREKNOWL'EDGE, a peculiar and essential attribute of God, referring to his knowledge of the future and of future events. Acts 2:23; Acts 15:18. Believers are said to be "elect according to the foreknowledge of God." 1 Pet 1:2.
entries.definition_ko: 하나님의 고유하고 본질적인 속성으로, 미래와 장래 사건에 대한 그분의 아심을 가리킨다(사도행전 2:23, 15:18). 신자들은 '하나님의 미리 아심을 따라 택하심을 받은' 자라 불린다(베드로전서 1:2).

entries.definition: FORERUN'NER. Heb 6:20. The term, as used of the entrance of our Saviour within the veil, refers to one who not only goes before to a particular place to make arrangements for his successors, but who leads or prepares the way.
entries.definition_ko: 히브리서 6:20에서 구주께서 휘장 안에 들어가심에 대해 쓰인 말로, 뒤따를 이들을 위해 준비하려 먼저 가는 이일 뿐 아니라 길을 이끌고 예비하는 이를 가리킨다.

entries.definition: FOR'EST. 1 Sam 22:5. Several tracts of country were designated in this way; as, "the forest of Hareth," that of "Ephraim," "the wood of Ziph," etc. It is known that in the tenth century a.d. there was a fir-wood between Jerusalem and Bethlehem. Not a trace of these forests remains. One of the chief causes of the present desolation of the Holy Land is the disappearance of forests. The "house of the forest of Lebanon," which was built by Solomon, and which was magnificent in size and style, 1 Kgs 7:2, was so called probably from the great quantity of cedar which was used in the construction of it.
entries.definition_ko: 여러 지역이 이렇게 불렸다(사무엘상 22:5) — '헤렛 수풀', '에브라임 수풀', '십 수풀' 등이다. AD 10세기에는 예루살렘과 베들레헴 사이에 잣나무 숲이 있었다고 알려져 있으나 지금은 그 흔적조차 없다. 성지가 오늘날 황폐해진 주된 원인 중 하나가 숲의 소멸이다. 솔로몬이 지은 '레바논 나무로 지은 집'(열왕기상 7:2)은 그 건축에 백향목이 많이 쓰였기에 그렇게 불린 듯하다.

entries.definition: FORGIVE'NESS is an act of God toward man, and of man toward his fellow. To forgive sin is the exclusive prerogative of God, of whose law sin is the transgression. Ps 130:4. Our Lord, by virtue of his divine nature, assumed the prerogative and exercised the power of forgiving sins, which the scribes and Pharisees, viewing him merely as a man, made the occasion of a charge of blasphemy, Mark 2:5. The gospel makes known not only that there is forgiveness with God, but also how such forgiveness is made compatible with the divine justice. Forgiveness, full, free, and everlasting, is offered to all who will believe and obey the gospel. Acts 13:38-39; 1 John 2:12. The duty of mutual forgiveness is urged upon man with the most solemn sanctions. Matt 6:14-15; Josh 18:22; Luke 17:3-4.
entries.definition_ko: 하나님이 사람에게, 또 사람이 이웃에게 행하는 일이다. 죄를 용서하는 것은 그 법을 어긴 대상인 하나님의 고유한 특권이다(시편 130:4). 주님은 신성으로 말미암아 이 특권을 취하시고 죄 사하는 권능을 행하셨는데, 그분을 한낱 사람으로만 본 서기관과 바리새인들은 이를 신성모독으로 고발했다(마가복음 2:5). 복음은 하나님께 용서가 있음뿐 아니라 그 용서가 어떻게 하나님의 공의와 조화되는지도 알려 준다. 충만하고 값없고 영원한 용서가 복음을 믿고 순종하는 모든 이에게 제시된다(사도행전 13:38-39, 요한일서 2:12). 서로 용서할 의무가 가장 엄중하게 촉구된다(마태복음 6:14-15, 누가복음 17:3-4).

entries.definition: FORKS, mentioned in 1 Sam 13:21, were used, not in eating (for the Orientals eat without forks), but in taking the meat out of the vessels in which it was cooked, or else in husbandry. See Eat, Eating.
entries.definition_ko: 사무엘상 13:21에 언급된 것으로, 식사에 쓴 것이 아니라(동방 사람은 포크 없이 먹는다) 삶은 그릇에서 고기를 건지거나 농사일에 쓴 것이다.

entries.definition: FORNICA'TION. This word, as used by the sacred writers, denotes various acts of lewdness and incontinency; and it is also figuratively applied to idolatry, or the mingling of the pure worship of God with the impure rites of heathenism. Matt 5:32, etc.
entries.definition_ko: 음행은 거룩한 기자들이 쓴 대로 여러 가지 음란하고 절제 없는 행위를 이른다. 또 빗대어 우상 섬김에도 쓰이니, 곧 하나님을 향한 순전한 예배에 이방 신앙의 더러운 예식을 섞는 것이다(마태복음 5:32).

entries.definition: FORSWEAR'. See Oath.
entries.definition_ko: 맹세 참조.

entries.definition: FORTUNA'TUS, one of the three Corinthians, the others being Stephanus and Achaieus, who were at Ephesus when Paul wrote his first Epistle to the Corinthians, and who are mentioned in the postscript as the bearers of the Epistles. 1 Cor 16:17.
entries.definition_ko: 바울이 고린도전서를 쓸 때 에베소에 있던 세 고린도 사람 중 하나로, 나머지는 스데바나와 아가이고다. 후기에 편지를 전한 자로 언급된다(고린도전서 16:17).

entries.definition: FOUNT'AIN. Springs of water are often mentioned in the Bible. Palestine, in contrast with Egypt, was a land of brooks of water, of fountains and depths, Deut 8:7. Hundreds of fountains may be counted with ease on either side of the Jordan. Some have peculiar properties. There are intermittent, thermal, brackish, sulphur, and hot springs. Perpetual fountains or springs of living water were greatly valued. Ps 36:8-9; Isa 49:10; Jer 2:13; Joel 3:18; Zech 13:1; John 4:10; Rev 7:17. In the expressive language of the Hebrews and the modern Arabs, a fountain is the "eye" of the locality. The importance of water is attested by the numerous names of localities into which enters the Hebrew en or the Arabic ain, "fountain," such as "En-rogel," "Engedi" (Arabic 'Ain-jidy), "En-had-dah." Damascus is the best supplied with water of all the Eastern cities; Jerusalem also had so abundant a supply that during its numerous sieges there was never a complaint on this score. Public fountains are frequent in the towns. The "fountain sealed" of Song 4:12 is a well-spring covered with a stone and sealed with the king's own signet. The word "fountain " was used figuratively; thus, Deut 33:28 and Ps 68:26, it is applied to Israel as the ancestor of the chosen people of God, and in Prov 5:18 to a beloved wife.
entries.definition_ko: 물의 샘이 성경에 자주 언급된다. 팔레스타인은 애굽과 달리 시내와 샘과 깊은 물의 땅이었다(신명기 8:7). 요단 양편에 수백 개의 샘을 쉽게 헤아릴 수 있다. 간헐천, 온천, 염천, 유황천 등 독특한 성질을 지닌 것도 있다. 끊이지 않는 생수의 샘은 매우 귀히 여겨졌다(시편 36:8-9, 이사야 49:10, 예레미야 2:13, 스가랴 13:1, 요한복음 4:10, 요한계시록 7:17). 히브리인과 오늘날 아랍인의 인상적인 표현으로 샘은 그 지역의 '눈'이다. 물의 중요함은 히브리어 '엔'이나 아랍어 '아인'('샘')이 들어간 수많은 지명이 증언한다 — 엔로겔, 엔게디, 엔핫다 등이다.

entries.definition: FOWL. See Bird.
entries.definition_ko: 새 참조.

entries.definition: FOX. Neh 4:3. Under this term the jackal is included — indeed, most of the references seem to be to that animal. The Orientals at the present time do not distinguish in common language between the two creatures. Both are common in Palestine. The fox (Vulpes vulgaris) is smaller than the jackal (Cam's aureus), and is of a reddish hue, while the latter is yellowish; hence its scientific name, meaning "the golden dog." It is the latter also, and not the fox, which devours the dead and follows armies that he may feed on human bodies left behind. Ps 63:10. Both animals are omnivorous, but the jackal, which goes in packs, is even more destructive to the vineyards than the other. Song 2:15. The crafty, artful nature of the fox is proverbial. Eze 13:4; Luke 13:32. He prowls singly for his prey of birds or small quadrupeds, which he takes by stratagem. Jackals are concealed by hundreds among the ruins, caves, and gardens of Syria. Lam 5:18. At sunset they come forth, and both then and at intervals through the night the traveller hears their cry, resembling the confused wailing of many infants. Evidently, the "foxes" which Samson The Syrian Fox. caught (Jud 15:4) were jackals. On this Tristram judiciously remarks: while Samson could not have caught so many foxes, "he might easily have 'snared,' as the Hebrew expresses it, 300 jackals, which hunt in large packs, and which are still most numerous in southern Palestine. It is not necessary to assume that the whole 300 were caught at once or turned loose in the same place, but rather that Samson, having taken them, turned them loose in many different places, so as to make 150 incendiary fires, and to cause the widest possible injury to the standing crops of the Philistines. The brands would be attached at some distance from the tails of the animals, and jackals, accustomed to run together, would not, unless very tightly fastened, pull in opposite directions, as foxes or dogs would; but the terrified animals would, so soon as ever they were let go, rush as fast as possible from their captor, and carry the devastation far and wide before the brand was extinguished." FRANKIN'CENSE (white), a dry, resinous, aromatic substance of a white or yellowish color, bitter and acrid to the taste, burning for a long time with a clear, steady, and very odoriferous flame. Several trees (of the genus Boswellia) which grow in India, Arabia, and Africa yield this gum from incisions in the bark. Along the coast of Hadramaut, a district of Arabia, as Carter has shown, frankincense (the olibanum of commerce) is produced, as was affirmed by Herodotus, Celsius, other ancient writers, and the Bible. Isa 60:6; Jer 6:20, The Arabian species (B. Carterii) somewhat resembles, especially in its Boswellia Thurifera. (Colehrooke. Supposed Frankincense. After Dr. Birdwood.) pinnate leaves when young, the mountain-ash. This gum, in the above and other passages, is mentioned simply as "incense." It is called frank because of the freeness with which it burns and gives forth its odors; and the pure incense is that which is first obtained, and is freest from foreign admixture. "Sweet incense," Ex 30:7, might as well be rendered "incense of spices," and is the composition mentioned in Ex 30:34. The use of incense in the Jewish worship may be learned from Ex 30:7 and Lev 16:12-13, and it is figuratively employed to represent lovely and agreeable qualities. Song 3:6; Song 4:6, Song 4:14, and devotional fervor. Ps 141:2; Mal 1:11;Rev 8:3. FRANK'LY is used in Luke 7:42 in the sense of "freely."
entries.definition_ko:
여우. 느헤미야 4장 3절이다. 이 말에는 자칼도 들어가니, 참으로 대부분의 대목이 그 짐승을 가리키는 듯하다. 오늘날 동방 사람들은 일상어에서 이 두 짐승을 구별하지 않는다. 둘 다 팔레스타인에 흔하다.

여우는 자칼보다 작고 불그스름한 빛깔인 반면, 자칼은 누르스름하다. 그래서 그 학명이 「금빛 개」라는 뜻이다. 죽은 것을 뜯어 먹고 뒤에 남은 사람의 주검을 먹으려고 군대를 따라다니는 것도 여우가 아니라 자칼이다. 시편 63편 10절이다.

두 짐승 다 무엇이든 먹으나, 떼 지어 다니는 자칼이 여우보다 포도원에 더 큰 해를 끼친다. 아가 2장 15절이다. 여우의 꾀바르고 교활한 성질은 널리 알려져 있다. 에스겔 13장 4절과 누가복음 13장 32절이다. 그것은 홀로 어슬렁거리며 새나 작은 네발짐승을 먹이로 노려 꾀로 잡는다.

자칼은 수리아의 폐허와 굴과 뜰에 수백 마리씩 숨어 있다. 예레미야애가 5장 18절이다. 해 질 무렵 그것들이 나오고, 그때와 밤중에 이따금 나그네는 그 울음을 듣는데 수많은 갓난아이가 어지러이 우는 소리 같다.

삼손이 잡은 「여우」는 분명히 자칼이었다. 사사기 15장 4절이다. 이에 대하여 트리스트럼은 슬기롭게 짚어 말한다. 삼손이 그토록 많은 여우를 잡을 수는 없었을 터이나, 「히브리어가 나타내는 대로 자칼 삼백 마리를 '덫으로 잡는' 일은 쉬웠을 것이다. 자칼은 큰 떼를 이루어 사냥하며 오늘도 팔레스타인 남부에 가장 많다. 삼백 마리를 한꺼번에 잡거나 같은 자리에 풀어놓았다고 여길 필요는 없다. 오히려 삼손이 그것들을 잡은 뒤 여러 다른 자리에 풀어놓아 백쉰 곳에 불을 지르고 블레셋 사람들의 선 곡식에 될 수 있는 대로 넓게 해를 입혔다고 보아야 한다. 홰는 짐승의 꼬리에서 얼마쯤 떨어뜨려 매었을 것이다. 그리고 함께 달리는 데 익숙한 자칼은 아주 단단히 매지 않는 한 여우나 개처럼 서로 반대쪽으로 당기지 않았을 것이다. 오히려 겁에 질린 짐승들은 풀려나자마자 잡은 이에게서 될 수 있는 대로 빨리 내달아, 홰가 꺼지기 전에 그 파괴를 멀리까지 퍼뜨렸을 것이다.」

유향. 「흰 것」이라는 뜻이며, 희거나 누르스름한 빛깔의 마르고 진 같은 향기로운 물질로서 맛이 쓰고 알알하며, 오래도록 맑고 고르고 매우 향기로운 불꽃으로 탄다. 인도와 아라비아와 아프리카에 자라는 여러 나무가 껍질에 낸 상처에서 이 진을 낸다.

아라비아의 한 지방인 하드라마우트 해안을 따라 유향이 나니, 카터가 밝힌 대로이며 헤로도토스와 켈시우스와 그 밖의 옛 저술가들과 성경이 그렇게 말한 바와 같다. 이사야 60장 6절과 예레미야 6장 20절이다. 아라비아 종은 특히 어릴 때의 깃꼴 잎이 마가목을 얼마쯤 닮았다.

이 진은 위의 대목과 그 밖의 대목에서 그냥 「향」으로 언급된다. 그것을 프랭크 곧 자유롭다 하는 것은 거리낌 없이 타며 향기를 내뿜기 때문이다. 그리고 순수한 향이란 처음 얻어져 다른 것이 섞이지 않은 것을 말한다.

출애굽기 30장 7절의 「향기로운 향」은 「향품의 향」으로 옮겨도 좋으며, 출애굽기 30장 34절에 언급된 조제품이다. 유대인의 예배에서 향을 어떻게 썼는지는 출애굽기 30장 7절과 레위기 16장 12절부터 13절까지에서 알 수 있다. 그리고 그것은 비유로 사랑스럽고 흡족한 성품을 나타내는 데 쓰이고, 아가 3장 6절과 아가 4장 6절과 아가 4장 14절이다, 또 경건의 뜨거움을 나타내는 데 쓰인다. 시편 141편 2절과 말라기 1장 11절과 요한계시록 8장 3절이다.

솔직히. 누가복음 7장 42절에서 「거저」라는 뜻으로 쓰였다.

「※ 원문 결함: 이 항목의 영문에는 여우 말고도 표제어 둘이 통째로 들어앉아 있다. 「유향」이 천사백 자 넘게, 이어서 「솔직히」가 붙어 있다. 그런데 「솔직히」는 바로 다음 항목으로 따로 있는 반면, 「유향」은 이 사전에 제 표제어가 아예 없다. 곧 유향을 표제어로 찾으면 나오지 않고 여우 항목 안에서만 볼 수 있다. 옮기지 않으면 그 내용이 통째로 사라지므로 영문 그대로 옮겼으나, 유향을 따로 항목으로 세울지는 판단이 필요하다.」

「※ 원문 결함: 영문 원문에서 도판 설명 둘이 문장 한가운데로 흘러들어 문장을 끊고 있다. 「삼손이 잡은 여우는 분명히 자칼이었다」 하는 문장 안에 「수리아 여우」가, 「아라비아 종은 마가목을 닮았다」 하는 문장 안에 「보스웰리아 투리페라. 콜브룩. 유향으로 여겨지는 것. 버드우드 박사를 따름」이 끼어들어 있다. 또한 예레미야 6장 20절 뒤에 마침표 자리에 쉼표가 찍혀 있다. 디지털화 과정에서 생긴 흠이며, 한글은 끊긴 문장을 이어 옮겼다.」

variants.definition: FOX. Neh 4:3. Under this term the jackal is included — indeed, most of the references seem to be to that animal. The Orientals at the present time do not distinguish in common language between the two creatures. Both are common in Palestine. The fox (Vulpes vulgaris) is smaller than the jackal (Cam's aureus), and is of a reddish hue, while the latter is yellowish; hence its scientific name, meaning "the golden dog." It is the latter also, and not the fox, which devours the dead and follows armies that he may feed on human bodies left behind. Ps 63:10. Both animals are omnivorous, but the jackal, which goes in packs, is even more destructive to the vineyards than the other. Song 2:15. The crafty, artful nature of the fox is proverbial. Eze 13:4; Luke 13:32. He prowls singly for his prey of birds or small quadrupeds, which he takes by stratagem. Jackals are concealed by hundreds among the ruins, caves, and gardens of Syria. Lam 5:18. At sunset they come forth, and both then and at intervals through the night the traveller hears their cry, resembling the confused wailing of many infants. Evidently, the "foxes" which Samson The Syrian Fox. caught (Jud 15:4) were jackals. On this Tristram judiciously remarks: while Samson could not have caught so many foxes, "he might easily have 'snared,' as the Hebrew expresses it, 300 jackals, which hunt in large packs, and which are still most numerous in southern Palestine. It is not necessary to assume that the whole 300 were caught at once or turned loose in the same place, but rather that Samson, having taken them, turned them loose in many different places, so as to make 150 incendiary fires, and to cause the widest possible injury to the standing crops of the Philistines. The brands would be attached at some distance from the tails of the animals, and jackals, accustomed to run together, would not, unless very tightly fastened, pull in opposite directions, as foxes or dogs would; but the terrified animals would, so soon as ever they were let go, rush as fast as possible from their captor, and carry the devastation far and wide before the brand was extinguished." FRANKIN'CENSE (white), a dry, resinous, aromatic substance of a white or yellowish color, bitter and acrid to the taste, burning for a long time with a clear, steady, and very odoriferous flame. Several trees (of the genus Boswellia) which grow in India, Arabia, and Africa yield this gum from incisions in the bark. Along the coast of Hadramaut, a district of Arabia, as Carter has shown, frankincense (the olibanum of commerce) is produced, as was affirmed by Herodotus, Celsius, other ancient writers, and the Bible. Isa 60:6; Jer 6:20, The Arabian species (B. Carterii) somewhat resembles, especially in its Boswellia Thurifera. (Colehrooke. Supposed Frankincense. After Dr. Birdwood.) pinnate leaves when young, the mountain-ash. This gum, in the above and other passages, is mentioned simply as "incense." It is called frank because of the freeness with which it burns and gives forth its odors; and the pure incense is that which is first obtained, and is freest from foreign admixture. "Sweet incense," Ex 30:7, might as well be rendered "incense of spices," and is the composition mentioned in Ex 30:34. The use of incense in the Jewish worship may be learned from Ex 30:7 and Lev 16:12-13, and it is figuratively employed to represent lovely and agreeable qualities. Song 3:6; Song 4:6, Song 4:14, and devotional fervor. Ps 141:2; Mal 1:11;Rev 8:3.
variants.definition_ko: 이 말에는 자칼이 포함되며, 실제로 대부분의 언급이 그 짐승을 가리키는 듯하다(느 4:3). 오늘날 동방 사람들도 일상어로 둘을 구별하지 않는다. 둘 다 팔레스타인에 흔하다. 여우는 자칼보다 작고 붉은빛을 띠며, 자칼은 누런빛이어서 학명이 '금빛 개'라는 뜻이다. 시체를 뜯어 먹고 군대를 따라다니며 버려진 주검을 먹는 것도 여우가 아니라 자칼이다(시 63:10). 둘 다 잡식성이나 무리 지어 다니는 자칼이 포도원에 더 해롭다(아 2:15). 여우의 교활함은 속담이 되어 있다(겔 13:4, 눅 13:32).

entries.definition: FRANK'LY is used in Luke 7:42 in the sense of "freely."
entries.definition_ko: 누가복음 7:42에서 '거저'라는 뜻으로 쓰인다.

entries.definition: FRIEND. Abraham is called "the friend of God." Isa 41:8; Jas 2:23. Jesus called his disciples his friends. John 15:15. He used a different word in the Greek to Judas, Matt 26:50, and one used more like our conventional "my good friend," implying kindly feeling, though no especial regard.
entries.definition_ko: 아브라함은 '하나님의 벗'이라 불린다(이사야 41:8, 야고보서 2:23). 예수께서 제자들을 자기 친구라 부르셨다(요한복음 15:15). 유다에게는 다른 헬라어를 쓰셨는데(마태복음 26:50), 우리의 통상적인 '이보시오'에 가까워 호의는 담겼으나 각별한 정은 없는 말이다.

entries.definition: FRIN'GES, a part of the outer garment, and the same as the hem or border of the garment. Deut 22:12; Matt 9:20; Matt 14:36. See Clothes. The children of Israel were enjoined to wear them by Moses, Num 15:38, and to place them on the four borders or edges of their outer garment, which was usually rectangular in shape. They were of a blue color. The object of the fringes was to remind the children of Israel of the commandments of God. Num 15:39. In the time of our Lord they had become objects of parade and show, so that he finds an evidence of the hypocrisy of the Pharisees in their practice of "enlarging the borders of their garments." The "hem of the garment" which the woman with the issue of blood touched. Matt 9:20, was the ancient fringe enjoined by Moses. They became with time, as did the rolls containing the Scriptures, phylacteries, and other things, objects of superstitious regard, and a Jewish commentator on Num. 15 says that any man clothed with this fringe is safe, and shall be delivered from all hurt and destruction.
entries.definition_ko: 옷단이니 겉옷의 한 부분이요 옷의 가와 같다(신명기 22:12; 마태복음 9:20; 마태복음 14:36). 옷 항목을 보라. 이스라엘 자손이 모세에게 그것을 달라는 명을 받았고(민수기 15:38), 대개 네모꼴이던 겉옷의 네 귀에 두라는 명을 받았다. 그것이 푸른 빛깔이었다. 옷단의 뜻은 이스라엘 자손에게 하나님의 계명을 일깨우는 것이었다(민수기 15:39). 우리 주 때에 그것이 뽐내고 내보이는 거리가 되어, 그가 바리새인이 「옷술을 길게 하는」 데에서 그 외식의 증거를 보신다. 혈루증 앓는 여인이 만진 「옷 가」는(마태복음 9:20) 모세가 명한 그 옛 옷단이었다. 성경을 담은 두루마리와 경문과 다른 것이 그러하였듯 이것도 때가 흐르며 미신다운 여김의 거리가 되었고, 민수기 15장에 대한 한 유대 주석가는 이 옷단을 입은 사람은 누구나 안전하고 온갖 해와 멸망에서 건져지리라 한다.

entries.definition: FROG, a well-known amphibious reptile which lives on insects, worms, etc. Ex 8:2. But one species is found in the waters of Egypt (Rana caculenia). In Rev 16:13 this creature is the symbol of uncleanness. Ex 8:2 records the miraculous multiplication of frogs among the Egyptians in such numbers as to fill their beds, ovens, and kneading-troughs; and when they died, as they did in immense masses, they filled the land with an offensive and pestilential effluvium.
entries.definition_ko: 벌레와 지렁이 등을 먹고 사는 잘 알려진 양서류다(출애굽기 8:2). 애굽의 물에는 한 종만 있다. 요한계시록 16:13에서는 부정함의 상징이다. 출애굽기 8:2은 개구리가 기적적으로 번성해 애굽 사람의 침상과 화덕과 떡 반죽 그릇을 가득 채웠고, 엄청난 무더기로 죽자 온 땅에 역겹고 병을 부르는 악취가 진동했음을 기록한다.

entries.definition: FRONT'LETS. See Phylacteries.
entries.definition_ko: 경문 참조.

entries.definition: FRUIT. The word is used in both a literal and figurative sense. "The fruit of the ground" is the product of the ground; "the fruit of the body" signifies children. By "fruit" is sometimes meant reward or consequences. Prov 1:31. "The fruit of the lips" is service or thanksgiving. But used literally it is a comprehensive term. For the regulation in regard to fruit trees, see Tree.
entries.definition_ko: 문자적으로도 비유적으로도 쓰인다. '땅의 소산'은 땅에서 나는 것이고, '몸의 소산'은 자녀를 뜻한다. '열매'는 때로 보응이나 결과를 뜻하며(잠언 1:31), '입술의 열매'는 섬김이나 감사를 뜻한다.

entries.definition: FU'EL was so scarce in the East that the people resorted to almost every kind of combustible matter, such as the withered stalks of herbs and flowers, Matt 6:28-30, thorns, Ps 58:9; Eccl 7:6, and even excrements. Eze 4:12-16. See Dung.
entries.definition_ko: 동방에는 땔감이 워낙 귀해 사람들이 시든 풀줄기와 꽃대(마태복음 6:28-30), 가시나무(시편 58:9, 전도서 7:6), 심지어 배설물(에스겔 4:12-16)까지 탈 만한 것은 거의 다 썼다. 똥 참조.

entries.definition: FULFIL'LED. Matt 2:17. This word is frequently used in reference to the accomplishment of prophecy. The expression, "that it might be fulfilled," Matt 2:15, 1 Chr 2:23; Lev 8:17; Heb 12:17, etc., etc., signifies that the events have fallen out in accordance with the prophecies of the O.T. The word in this connection is almost synonymous with "verified." In other connections. Gen 25:24; Rev 15:8, etc., the word means "completed" or "accomplished," as when Christ said, "The time is fulfilled," Mark 1:15.
entries.definition_ko:
예언의 성취와 관련해 자주 쓰인다(마태복음 2:17). '이루려 하심이라'(마태복음 2:15)는 그 일이 구약의 예언대로 일어났음을 뜻하며, 이런 맥락에서는 '확증되었다'와 거의 같은 뜻이다. 다른 맥락에서는(창세기 25:24, 요한계시록 15:8) '완료되다', '성취되다'를 뜻하니, 그리스도께서 '때가 찼고' 하신 것과 같다(마가복음 1:15).
※ 원문 오류: 1 Chr 2:23 → 마태복음 2:23
※ 판정 근거: 이어받기 숫자 부풀리기. 원문에서 책과 장을 생략한 맨 숫자에 엉뚱한 주소가 붙은 것이다. 앞의 성한 인용을 좇으면 마태복음 2:23가 되며, 그 절은 「나사렛이란 동네에 가서 사니 이는 선지자로 하신 말씀에 나사렛 사람이라…」이다.

entries.definition: FUL'LER. The Hebrew word comes from the verb "to tread," because originally the clothing was trodden upon in tubs of water until the soap which had been dissolved had cleansed it. The fuller did not simply full new cloth, but washed clothing that had been worn. Among the primitive Hebrews washing was done at home by the women. Ex 19:10; Num 19:7. It was obligatory in the case of the leper's clothing. Lev 13:54. But in later times among the Hebrews, as among the Egyptians, as the monuments testify, washing was an especial and important business of the men. 2 Kgs 18:17; Isa 7:3; Isa 36:2; Mark 9:3. Mention is made in the Bible of the various substances used in this business, such as nitre, Prov 26:20; Jer 2:22; soap, probably the juice of some saponaceous plant, Mal 3:2. Chalk was rubbed into clothes for the same purpose. Since the fullers occasioned offensive smells, they carried on their work outside the cities. West of Jerusalem was their field; its removed position and the supply of water from the upper Pool of Gihon rendered the place very fit. See Fullers' Field. En-rogel was the fullers' fountain.
entries.definition_ko: 히브리어는 '밟다'라는 동사에서 왔는데, 본래 옷을 물통에 넣고 녹인 비누로 밟아 씻었기 때문이다. 세탁자는 새 천을 마무르기만 한 것이 아니라 입던 옷도 빨았다. 초기 히브리인 사이에서는 여인들이 집에서 빨래를 했다(출애굽기 19:10, 민수기 19:7). 나병환자의 옷은 반드시 빨아야 했다(레위기 13:54). 그러나 후대에는 애굽에서처럼 남자들의 중요한 전문 직업이 되었다(열왕기하 18:17, 이사야 7:3, 마가복음 9:3). 잿물(잠언 25:20, 예레미야 2:22)과 비누, 아마도 어떤 비누 성분 식물의 즙(말라기 3:2)이 쓰였고 백묵도 옷에 문질렀다. 냄새가 고약해 성 밖에서 일했다.

entries.definition: FUL'LERS' FIELD, a spot close to the walls of Jerusalem, 2 Kgs 18:17, 2 Kgs 18:26; Isa 36:2; 1 Kgs 7:3. One resort of the fullers appears to have been En-rogel, below and south-east of Jerusalem, but the place where Rabshakeh stood was probably on the north of the city, or perhaps near the Jaffa gate, at the upper Gihon pool, where fullers now whiten their garments.
entries.definition_ko: 예루살렘 성벽에 가까운 곳이다(열왕기하 18:17,26, 이사야 36:2, 7:3). 세탁자들이 자주 찾은 곳 하나가 예루살렘 남동쪽 아래의 엔로겔이었던 듯하나, 랍사게가 섰던 곳은 성 북쪽, 아마도 지금 세탁자들이 옷을 희게 하는 윗못 근처였을 것이다.

entries.definition: FULLNESS. Gal 4:4. This expression has a peculiar meaning in some passages of the sacred writings. The "fulness of time," in relation to the Messiah, has the same meaning as the expression "when the measure of time was full" -that is, when the time had elapsed as appointed by God, and all the preparations for his coming were completed. So when the day of Pentecost was fully come. Acts 2:1. The same word is used, John 1:16 and Col 1:19, to signify the perfect and complete sufficiency of spiritual blessings in Christ Jesus. "Fulness of the Godhead," Col 2:9, denotes all the attributes of the divine nature in their entire and complete perfection. The "fulness of Deity" was in Christ.
entries.definition_ko: 이 표현은 성경 몇 곳에서 독특한 뜻을 지닌다(갈라디아서 4:4). 메시아와 관련한 '때가 차매'는 '시간의 분량이 찼을 때', 곧 하나님이 정하신 때가 지나고 그분의 오심을 위한 모든 준비가 마쳐졌음을 뜻한다. 오순절 날이 '이미 이르매'도 마찬가지다(사도행전 2:1). 같은 말이 요한복음 1:16과 골로새서 1:19에서 그리스도 예수 안에 있는 영적 복의 완전하고 온전한 충족을 뜻하는 데 쓰인다. '신성의 충만'(골로새서 2:9)은 신적 본성의 모든 속성이 온전하고 완전함을 나타낸다.

entries.definition: FU'NERAL. See Bury.
entries.definition_ko: 장례 참조.

entries.definition: FUR'LONG. See Measures.
entries.definition_ko: 도량형 참조.

entries.definition: FUR'NACE. Furnaces were used for melting the precious metals. Prov 17:3. They were also used to punish criminals. The furnace into which Nebuchadnezzar cast the young Hebrews who refused to worship his image, Dan 3:22-23; cf. Jer 29:22, was probably a large furnace, like a brick kiln, with an opening at the top to cast in the materials; a second, for the removal of slag, cinders, etc., or molten Egyptian Furnace. (Ayre.) metal, was arranged below, in one of the sides, so that the material in the interior could be observed.
entries.definition_ko: 귀금속을 녹이는 데 풀무불을 썼다(잠언 17:3). 죄인을 벌하는 데도 쓰였다. 느부갓네살이 자기 신상에 절하기를 거부한 히브리 청년들을 던져 넣은 풀무는(다니엘 3:22-23, 예레미야 29:22) 벽돌 가마 같은 큰 것으로, 재료를 넣는 구멍이 위에 있고 찌꺼기와 재나 녹은 금속을 꺼내는 두 번째 구멍이 아래 옆면에 있어 안의 상태를 볼 수 있었을 것이다.

entries.definition: FUR'NITURE. To a European eye the best-furnished houses in the East appear empty. On the marble floors are rugs, on the divan are cushions of rich materials. But the great variety of furniture to which we are accustomed is unknown. The poor of course had correspondingly less. A mat or a skin to recline on during the day, a mattress to sleep on at night, a stool, a little low table, and a brazier, — this would be the extent of the furniture. It is interesting to observe that the rich Shunammite furnished the room of Elisha with simply a bed — perhaps merely a mattress — a table, a stool (chair), and a candlestick. 2 Kgs 4:10-13. The word "furniture" is used in Gen 31:34 of the camel-trappings.
entries.definition_ko: 유럽인의 눈에는 동방에서 가장 잘 갖춘 집도 비어 보인다. 대리석 바닥에 깔개가 있고 긴 의자에 값진 방석이 놓여 있을 뿐, 우리에게 익숙한 다양한 가구는 없다. 가난한 이는 그만큼 더 적었다. 낮에 기대어 쉴 자리나 가죽, 밤에 잘 요, 걸상 하나, 작고 낮은 상 하나, 화로 하나 — 이것이 가구의 전부였을 것이다. 부유한 수넴 여인이 엘리사의 방에 침상과 상과 걸상과 촛대만 갖추어 준 것이 흥미롭다(열왕기하 4:10). 창세기 31:34에서는 낙타의 안장 기구를 가리킨다.

entries.definition: FURROW is the translation of different words in the Hebrew. In Hos 10:10 the word is properly "transgressions." The complaining of the furrows. Job 31:38, is mentioned in Hindoo proverbs.
entries.definition_ko: 여러 히브리어를 옮긴 말이다. 호세아 10:10에서는 본래 '허물'이다. 밭이랑이 부르짖는다는 표현(욥기 31:38)은 힌두 속담에도 나온다.

entries.definition: FU'RY. Jer 10:25. As the word is generally used, the prophet here attributes to God what is true only of man. We associate haste, impulse, thoughtlessness, and unkindness with fury. But in this sense God cannot have the emotion of fury. He has anger for sin, but this is a righteous and holy feeling, devoid of the bitterness by which men are most often actuated in their fury; and when he is said to pour out his fury on a person or on a people, it is a figurative expression for dispensing afflictive judgments. Modern Eastern Furniture. 1. A Village Table. 2. A Brazier, Tongs, etc. 3. Chairs, Persian Canopy Bed, a Couch and Wooden Pillow.
entries.definition_ko: 예레미야 10:25. 이 말이 일반적으로 쓰이는 뜻대로라면 선지자는 사람에게만 참인 것을 하나님께 돌리는 셈이다. 우리는 분노에 성급함과 충동, 무분별과 몰인정을 결부시킨다. 그러나 그런 뜻에서 하나님은 진노의 감정을 지니실 수 없다. 죄에 대한 노여움은 있으시나, 이는 의롭고 거룩한 감정으로 사람이 분노할 때 흔히 지니는 쓰디쓴 마음이 없다. 그분이 어떤 사람이나 백성에게 진노를 쏟으신다 할 때는 괴로운 심판을 내리신다는 비유적 표현이다.

entries.definition: GA'AL (loathing), the son of Ebed, led a revolt against Abimelech, king of the Shechemites. Jer Jud, 9:26-46. He was defeated and his partisans were scattered.
entries.definition_ko: 에벳의 아들로 세겜 사람들의 왕 아비멜렉에 맞서 반역을 이끌었다(사사기 9:26-46). 패하여 그 무리가 흩어졌다.

entries.definition: GA'ASH (earthquake), the hill where Joshua was buried. Josh 24:30; Jud 2:9. South of Tibneh, which is identified as Timnath-serah, is a hill, upon the north side of which are tombs; hence it is supposed to be " the hill Gaash."
entries.definition_ko: 여호수아가 묻힌 산이다(여호수아 24:30, 사사기 2:9). 딤낫세라로 확인된 티브네 남쪽에 언덕이 있고 그 북쪽 면에 무덤들이 있어 '가아스 산'으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: GA'BA. See Geba.
entries.definition_ko: 게바 참조.

entries.definition: GAB'BAI (tax-gatherer), a Benjamite living in Jerusalem. Neh 11:8.
entries.definition_ko: 예루살렘에 살던 베냐민 사람(느헤미야 11:8).

entries.definition: GAB'BATHA (platform), the place of Pilate's judgment-seat; called also "the pavement." John 19:13. The judgment-hall was the Praetorium, on the western hill of Jerusalem, and the pavement, or Gabbatha, was a tesselated pavement outside the hall.
entries.definition_ko: 빌라도의 재판석이 있던 곳으로 '박석'이라고도 불린다(요한복음 19:13). 재판정은 예루살렘 서쪽 언덕의 관정이었고, 박석 곧 가바다는 그 밖의 모자이크 포장 자리였다.

entries.definition: GA'BRIEL (man of God), an angel specially charged with the message to Zacharias respecting the birth of John, and to Mary respecting the birth of Christ. Luke 1:19-26. At an earlier period he was sent to Daniel to unfold a vision. Dan 8:16; Dan 9:21. See Angels.
entries.definition_ko: '하나님의 사람'이라는 뜻으로, 사가랴에게 요한의 출생을, 마리아에게 그리스도의 출생을 알리는 사명을 특별히 맡은 천사다(누가복음 1:19,26). 그 전에는 다니엘에게 보내져 환상을 풀어 주었다(다니엘 8:16, 9:21). 천사 참조.

entries.definition: GAD, THE TRIBE OF. The territory, given to the tribe of Gad lay east of the Jordan, north of that allotted to Reuben, and south of that given to Manasseh on that side of the river. It extended from the Jordan eastward to Aroer, Josh 13:25, including half of Mount Gilead and half of Ammon. Deut 3:12; Josh 13:25. For physical features and history, see Gilead. Its chief cities were Ramoth-gilead, Mahanaim, Heshbon, and Aroer. This tribe, in the Wilderness, was placed with Simeon and Reuben on the south of the tabernacle; with Reuben and the half of Manasseh, it occupied the pasture-grounds on the east of the Jordan. It was warlike, as is graphically stated, 1 Chr 12:8. Two famous men came from Gad — Barzillai, 2 Sam 17:27, and Elijah, 1 Kgs 17:1. The territory was the battle-field for wars between Syria and Israel. 2 Kgs 10:33.
entries.definition_ko: 갓 지파이다. 갓 지파에게 준 땅이 요단 동쪽, 르우벤에게 나누어 준 것의 북쪽이요 그 강 저편에서 므낫세에게 준 것의 남쪽에 놓였다. 그것이 요단에서 동쪽으로 아로엘까지 뻗었고(여호수아 13:25) 길르앗 산의 절반과 암몬의 절반을 아울렀다(신명기 3:12; 여호수아 13:25). 자연의 모습과 역사는 길르앗 항목을 보라. 그 으뜸 성읍은 길르앗 라못과 마하나임과 헤스본과 아로엘이었다. 이 지파가 광야에서 시므온과 르우벤과 함께 성막 남쪽에 두어졌고, 르우벤과 므낫세 반 지파와 함께 요단 동쪽의 목초지를 차지하였다. 역대상 12:8에 생생히 적힌 대로 싸움에 능하였다. 갓에서 이름난 두 사람이 났으니 바르실래(사무엘하 17:27)와 엘리야이다(열왕기상 17:1). 이 땅이 아람과 이스라엘 사이 싸움의 터였다(열왕기하 10:33).

variants.definition: GAD (good fortune ?). The seventh son of Jacob, and the first-born of Zilpah, Leah's handmaid, Gen 30:11. A prophet and particular friend of David, the history of whose reign he wrote. 1 Chr 29:29. He came to David when the latter was in the cave Adullam. 1 Sam 22:5. He then began his career of counsellor, under divine direction, which eventually won him the title of "the king's seer." 2 Sam 24:11, 2 Sam 24:13; 1 Chr 21:9. In Hezekiah's day he was remembered. 2 Chr 29:25.
variants.definition_ko: 1) 야곱의 일곱째 아들이자 레아의 여종 실바의 맏아들(창 30:11). 2) 선지자이자 다윗의 각별한 벗으로 그 치세의 역사를 기록했다(대상 29:29). 다윗이 아둘람 굴에 있을 때 그에게 왔고(삼상 22:5), 그때부터 하나님의 지시를 따라 조언하는 일을 시작해 마침내 '왕의 선견자'라는 칭호를 얻었다(삼하 24:11).

variants.definition_ko: 갓 지파에게 주어진 땅은 요단 동편, 르우벤 몫의 북쪽, 므낫세 몫의 남쪽에 있었다. 요단에서 동쪽으로 아로엘까지 뻗어(여호수아 13:25) 길르앗산의 절반과 암몬의 절반을 포함했다(신명기 3:12). 주요 성읍은 라못길르앗, 마하나임, 헤스본, 아로엘이었다. 광야에서 이 지파는 시므온, 르우벤과 함께 성막 남쪽에 자리했다. 호전적인 지파였으며(역대상 12:8) 바르실래(사무엘하 17:27)와 엘리야(열왕기상 17:1) 두 유명한 인물이 갓에서 나왔다. 이 땅은 시리아와 이스라엘 사이 전쟁터가 되었다(열왕기하 10:33).

entries.definition: GAD'ARA. See Gadarenes.
entries.definition_ko: 가다라 사람 참조.

entries.definition: GAD'ARENES, COUNTRY OF, possibly the same as that of the Gergesenes. Matt 8:28; Mark 5:1; Luke 8:26. A region about Gadara, an important city about 6 miles south-east of the Sea of Galilee, and 16 miles from Tiberias; now called Um Keis. The town is about 1215 feet above the sea level, on the western crest of a mountain. The tomb-caverns are very numerous, and some of them are still inhabited by the Arabs, illustrating Matt 8:28. The ruins of the ancient city cover a circuit of about 2 miles, including a street with basalt pavement having marks of chariot-wheels. There are rows of columns, two theatres. The place of the miracle of Matt 8:28-33 has been in doubt, but it cannot be Gadara, which is too far from the lake for the herd of swine to rush into it precipitantly in one short movement. Recent explorations fix it, with some certainty, about midway of the Lake of Galilee, on its eastern side and near Gerasa, or modern Kersa. Between two wadys, Seniakh and Fik, which are 3 miles apart, the hills come within 40 feet of the lake, and present a steep slope, so that a herd of swine running swiftly down it would be carried on into the water. This identification is supported by W. M. Thomson, Tristram, and the members of the Palestine Exploration Survey. W. M. Thomson suggests that Matthew, writing for the Hebrews, who knew the country, notices the more exact but less known locality of Gergesa, while Mark and Luke, writing for those at a distance, refer simply to the country of Gadara, which was more widely known as the capital of that region,
entries.definition_ko: 가다라 지방이니 아마 거라사 지방과 같을 것이다(마태복음 8:28; 마가복음 5:1; 누가복음 8:26). 가다라 언저리의 지역이니, 가다라는 갈릴리 바다 남동쪽 육 마일, 디베랴에서 십육 마일의 중요한 성이요 지금 움 케이스라 한다. 이 성읍이 바다보다 천이백십오 피트 높은 한 산의 서쪽 마루에 있다. 무덤 굴이 매우 많고 그 얼마에 아직 아랍 사람이 사니, 마태복음 8:28을 밝혀 준다. 옛 성의 폐허가 둘레 이 마일쯤을 덮고, 병거 바퀴 자국이 있는 현무암 포장 거리와 줄지은 기둥과 극장 둘이 있다. 마태복음 8:28-33의 이적이 있은 곳이 의심되어 왔으나 가다라일 수 없으니, 돼지 떼가 짧은 한 달음에 내리달아 들기에는 호수에서 너무 멀기 때문이다. 최근의 조사가 그것을 얼마쯤 확실히 갈릴리 호수 동쪽 한가운데쯤, 거라사 곧 오늘의 케르사 가까이로 정한다. 삼 마일 떨어진 두 와디 세미아크와 피크 사이에서 언덕이 호수에서 사십 피트 안까지 다가오며 가파른 비탈을 이루니, 돼지 떼가 빠르게 내리달으면 물로 실려 갈 것이다. 이 밝힘을 톰슨과 트리스트럼과 팔레스타인 탐사대의 지체들이 뒷받침한다. 톰슨은, 마태가 이 나라를 아는 히브리 사람을 위하여 쓰므로 더 정확하나 덜 알려진 거라사의 자리를 짚고, 마가와 누가는 멀리 있는 이를 위하여 쓰므로 그 지역의 서울로 더 널리 알려진 가다라 지방만을 가리킨다고 여긴다.

A region about Gadara, an important city about 6 miles south-east of the Sea of Galilee, and 16 miles from Tiberias; now called Um Keis. The town is about 1215 feet above the sea level, on the western crest of a mountain. The tomb-caverns are very numerous, and some of them are still inhabited by the Arabs, illustrating Matt 8:28. The ruins of the ancient city cover a circuit of about 2 miles, including a street with basalt pavement having marks of chariot-wheels. There are rows of columns, two theatres. The place of the miracle of Matt 8:28-33 has been in doubt, but it cannot be Gadara, which is too far from the lake for the herd of swine to rush into it precipitantly in one short movement. Recent explorations fix it, with some certainty, about midway of the Lake of Galilee, on its eastern side and near Gerasa, or modern Kersa. Between two wadys, Seniakh and Fik, which are 3 miles apart, the hills come within 40 feet of the lake, and present a steep slope, so that a herd of swine running swiftly down it would be carried on into the water. This identification is supported by W. M. Thomson, Tristram, and the members of the Palestine Exploration Survey. W. M. Thomson suggests that Matthew, writing for the Hebrews, who knew the country, notices the more exact but less known locality of Gergesa, while Mark and Luke, writing for those at a distance, refer simply to the country of Gadara, which was more widely known as the capital of that region,

entries.definition: GALA'TIA, a central province of Asia Minor, subject to the Roman rule, bounded by Bithynia and Paphlagonia on the north, Pontus on the east, Cappadocia and Lycaonia on the south, and Phrygia on the west. Its boundaries, however, were often changed. In Ptolemy's time it extended to the Euxine or Black Sea, and at one time included Lycaonia on the south. Its capitals were Tavium, Pessinus, and Ancyra. The country is chiefly high tableland between the two rivers Halys and Sangarius. The Galatians were originally Gauls or Celts who 300 years before Christ moved from the regions of the Rhine back toward the east, and there mingled with Greeks and Jews. Their character resembled that of the modern French, and combined quick temper, prompt action, inconstancy, and changeableness. So they appear in the Epistle of Paul to them. Galatia was a part of Paul's missionary-field. He visited it once with Silas and Timothy, Acts 16:6; again, on his third tour, he "went over all the country of Galatia," Acts 18:23, and received a collection for the saints from its churches, 1 Cor 16:1. Crescens also appears to have been sent there near the close of Paul's life. 2 Tim 4:10.
entries.definition_ko: 로마의 지배 아래 있던 소아시아 중앙의 속주로, 북쪽은 비두니아와 바블라고니아, 동쪽은 본도, 남쪽은 갑바도기아와 루가오니아, 서쪽은 브루기아와 접했다. 경계는 자주 바뀌어 프톨레마이오스 때는 흑해까지 뻗었다. 수도는 타비움, 페시누스, 앙카라였다. 할리스 강과 상가리우스 강 사이의 높은 고원 지대다. 갈라디아 사람은 본래 갈리아인, 곧 켈트족으로 그리스도보다 300년 전 라인강 유역에서 동쪽으로 옮겨 와 헬라인·유대인과 섞였다. 성격은 오늘날 프랑스인과 비슷해 급한 성미와 재빠른 행동, 변덕과 변하기 쉬움이 뒤섞여 있으며 바울의 편지에서도 그렇게 나타난다. 바울의 선교지 일부로, 실라와 디모데와 함께 한 번 방문했고(사도행전 16:6) 세 번째 여행 때 '갈라디아 온 땅을 두루 다녔다'.

entries.definition: GALATIANS, EPISTLE TO, written by Paul with his own hand (ch. Gal 6:11) between a.d. 65-58. Its design is to diffuse true notions among the Galatian Christians concerning justification, the relation of the Mosaic economy to the Christian, and the authority of Paul as an apostle. The Galatians had received Paul with much enthusiasm when he first preached the gospel to them, Gal 4:15. After his departure teachers had disseminated the false idea that the obligation was incumbent upon the followers of Christ to practise the ceremonies and rites of the Mosaic code. With much vehemence and fervor Paul combats their Judaizing teachings, and enforces the doctrine that by faith alone are we justified. Faith constitutes one the child of Abraham, Lev 3:9, and circumcision is not only not essential to salvation, but is in itself of no avail. 1 Kgs 6:6. Chs. 1 and 2 are occupied mainly with a vindication of Paul's apostolic commission as of equal authority with that of the other apostles, and with an account of a debate concerning meats at the council of Jerusalem. Chs. 5 and 6 contain practical exhortations. The main argument, that we become partakers of salvation by faith, Gal 3:26, is the same in the Epistle to the Galatians as in that to the Romans. The two Epistles were best understood in the time of the Reformation, and form the magna charta of evangelical Protestantism.
entries.definition_ko: 갈라디아서이니 바울이 제 손으로 썼고(갈라디아서 6:11) 주후 55년과 58년 사이의 것이다. 그 뜻은 칭의와 모세의 경륜이 그리스도의 경륜에 대하여 지니는 관계와 사도로서의 바울의 권위에 대하여, 갈라디아 그리스도인 가운데 바른 생각을 퍼뜨리려는 것이다. 갈라디아 사람이 바울이 처음 복음을 전할 때에 그를 큰 열심으로 맞았다(갈라디아서 4:15). 그가 떠난 뒤에 어떤 스승들이 그리스도를 따르는 이가 모세의 법의 예식과 의례를 지킬 의무가 있다는 거짓 생각을 퍼뜨렸다. 바울이 크게 힘차고 뜨겁게 그 유대주의의 가르침을 거스르고, 오직 믿음으로만 우리가 의롭다 하심을 얻는다는 가르침을 힘 있게 말한다. 믿음이 사람을 아브라함의 자녀 되게 하고, 할례가 구원에 꼭 필요하지 않을 뿐 아니라 그 자체로 아무 쓸데가 없다. 1장과 2장이 주로 바울의 사도의 사명이 다른 사도들의 것과 같은 권위를 지님을 밝히는 데에, 또 예루살렘 회의에서 먹는 것을 두고 벌어진 논쟁의 기록에 쓰인다. 5장과 6장이 실천의 권함을 담는다. 우리가 믿음으로 구원에 참여하게 된다는 으뜸 논지가(갈라디아서 3:26) 갈라디아서와 로마서에 같다. 이 두 편지가 종교개혁 때에 가장 잘 알아들어졌고, 복음다운 개신교의 대헌장을 이룬다.

entries.definition: GAL'BANUM, a resinous gum of dark-yellow color, produced in Syria and neighboring countries, Ex 30:34. It burns with a pungent, disagreeable odor, was an ingredient of the sacred incense, and is still valued for its medicinal properties. There is uncertainty from what plant it is obtained, but that of Palestine is thought to be from one which botanists call Galbanum officinale.

entries.definition: GALILEE, SEA OF, a small lake of deep interest to the Bible-reader as the scene of some of the most remarkable works of Jesus. The lake is named from the district or province of Galilee. It was known by several other names, as the sea of Chinnereth, Num 34:11; Deut 3:17, or Chinneroth. Josh 11:2; 1 Chr 12:3, or Cinneroth, 1 Kgs 15:20, probably from a town of that name which stood on its shore. Josh 19:35; the lake of Gennesaret, Luke 5:1, from the plain or land of that name on its north-western side. Matt 14:34; Mark 6:53; the sea of Tiberias, from the celebrated city of that name, John 6:1; and the sea, Matt 4:15. It is also called Gennesar in the Apocryjphal book of Maccabees, 1 Mace. 11:67. Its present name is Bahr Tabariyeh. It is worthy of note that all the towns whose names were applied to this lake were situated upon its western side. "Gennezareth," which is a form of the name also given to the sea by many authors, is not found in the A.V. of our English Bible. Situation and Extent. — This sea is 60 miles north-east from Jerusalem, and 27 east of the Mediterranean Sea. Its form is an irregular oval or pear-shape, the broad end being toward the north. Its length is 12 1/2 miles according to Wilson, 16 1/2 according to Baedeker, and its breadth from 4 to 7 1/2 miles. Its level varies at different seasons, and is from 600 to 700 feet below the Mediterranean, the mean depression being about 626 feet, and its depth 160 feet. Physical Features. — The lake is surrounded by an almost continuous wall of hills, broken or receding occasionally, as at Tiberias, the plain of Gennesaret, and at the Jordan. The hills are of limestone, basalt, and volcanic rocks, indications of volcanic action being also specially abundant in the Jordanic chasm, though Wilson sees nothing to indicate a volcanic origin of the lake. Hot springs abound; earthquakes are frequent. The Jordan runs through the lake, coloring its water for a mile. The water of the lake is slightly salty, but drunk by the people. Fish abound, many species having been found. Tristram says: "The shoals were marvellous black masses of many hundred yards long, with the black fins projecting out of the water as thickly as they could pack. No wonder that any net should break which enclosed such a shoal! Yet though the lake swarms with fish as I could not have believed water could swarm, there are but two boats existing on its whole extent besides a ferry-boat." (Land of Israel, p. 430.) Baedeker notes three miserable fishing-boats. These are all that are left to remind the traveller of the numerous boats which our Saviour saw on the Sea of Galilee. Josephus describes a naval engagement which took place on its waters between the Jews and the soldiers of Vespasian. Violent and Sketch-Map of the Sea of Galilee. (Palestine Exploration Fund.) sudden storms are common now on the lake, as in our Lord's day. Scripture History. — This lake is mentioned in the O.T. but seldom, and then rather incidentally, as in Num 34:11; Deut 3:17; Josh 11:2; 1 Chr 12:3; 1 Kgs 15:20. Its chief interest is its association with the public ministry of our Saviour. Upon its shores was "his own city," Matt 9:1; from fishing-boats on Galilee he called Simon Peter and his brother Andrew, and his partners James and John, who were thenceforth "to catch men," Matt 4:18,Matt 4:22; Mark 1:16-20; Luke 5:1-11; on it he stilled the tempest and made the winds and the sea obev him. Matt 8:23-27; Matt 14:22-33; see also Matt 17:27; Mark 7:31-35; at the Sea of Tiberias Christ also showed himself to the disciples after his resurrection. John 21. Of the nine or more populous cities which stood upon its shores, the more important were Bethsaida, Capernaum, Chorazin, Tiberias, and Magdala. Present Appearance. — Porter gives an eloquent description of the lake as it appeared to him from his tent-door, on a lovely spot, at evening: " The silence was profound. Even Nature seemed to have fallen asleep. The river glided noiselessly past; the sea was spread before me like a polished mirror. . . . East of the lake the side of Bashan's lofty plateau rose as a mountain-chain, and at its northern end my eye rested on the very scene of that miracle of mercy where thousands were fed, and at its southern end on that of the miracle of judgment, where 'the whole herd of swine ran violently down a steep place, and perished in the waters.' Away to the west the shattered ramparts of Tiberias seemed to rise out of the bosom of the lake, and behind them a dark mountain, in whose caverned cliffs repose the ashes of many a learned rabbin, while over all appeared the graceful rounded top of Tabor. Farther to the right, on the white strand, I saw the huts of Magdala, with the coast of Gennesaret extending from it northward to Capernaum — Christ's own city." At the present time the lake is almost utterly forsaken: only three or four fisher-boats can be found there; while at the time of Christ it was covered with sailing-vessels, and the surrounding western shore (the plain of Gennesaret) was, according to the glowing description of Josephus, a paradise of beauty and fertility. F.R. and C.R. Conder describe the famous sea as pear-shaped, and resembling in size the English lake Windermere. They add: "It is surrounded with precipices of limestone, except on the north, where a shelving slope leads to the shore from a plateau of basalt extending from the foot of the highest range of Upper Galilee. The scenery of the lake is bare, and much tamer The Sea of Galilee from Tiberias. (After original Photograph.) than that of the Dead Sea. The beach is narrow except on the north-west, where the cliffs recede, leaving a fertile plain (Gennesaret), 2 1/2 miles long and 1 mile broad, watered by several fine springs. The pebbly open shore on the north is broken into numerous bays, and is fringed with dark oleander bushes. On the south-eastern side is a palm-grove, and a few palms dot the western shore. The ruddy cliffs on the west and the steep slopes on the east are bare and desolate, but the sweet waters of the lake, in calm weather mirroring the surrounding hills and shining in the sun, present a beautiful scene, especially at evening. The sea is remarkable for its shoals of fish, for the violence of its sudden thunder-storms, and for the hot springs along its shores. The neighborhood of the lake is also peculiarly subject to volcanic disturbances." —Handbook of the Bible, p. 215 (1879). The Rev. Dr. S. Manning encountered a sudden and violent storm on this lake, illustrating many of the details of N.T. history: "I had taken a boat, on a bright, cloudless morning, to explore the eastern shores and the point where the Jordan enters the lake. There was not a ripple on the water, not a perceptible current in the air. Almost without warning, the wind rose: the waves, crested with foam, began to break over the sides of the boat. I was sitting on a cushion, or 'pillow,' on the flat, raised stern, 'in the hinder part of the ship,' and watched the crew 'toiling and rowing.' But all their efforts were in vain. They were unable to make any way, for 'the wind was contrary.' At length one of them jumped overboard, and, partly swimming, partly wading, towed the vessel ashore." —Holy Fields, p. 205. Capt. Wilson experienced a similar sudden storm.
entries.definition_ko:
갈릴리 바다이니, 예수의 더없이 남다른 일 가운데 얼마의 무대로서 성경 읽는 이에게 깊은 관심을 주는 작은 호수이다. 이 호수는 갈릴리 지역 곧 지방에서 이름을 얻었다. 다른 여러 이름으로도 알려졌으니, 긴네렛 바다(민수기 34:11; 신명기 3:17) 곧 긴네롯(여호수아 11:2; 역대상 12:3) 곧 긴느롯이며(열왕기상 15:20) 아마 그 기슭에 섰던 그 이름의 성읍에서 왔을 것이다(여호수아 19:35). 게네사렛 호수라 하니(누가복음 5:1) 그 북서쪽의 그 이름의 벌판 곧 땅에서 왔고(마태복음 14:34; 마가복음 6:53), 디베랴 바다라 하니 그 이름난 성에서 왔으며(요한복음 6:1), 그저 바다라고도 한다(마태복음 4:15). 외경 마카베오서에서는 게네사르라 한다(마카베오상 11:67). 오늘 이름은 바흐르 타바리예이다. 이 호수에 붙은 이름의 성읍이 다 그 서쪽에 자리 잡았음이 짚을 만하다. 여러 저술가가 이 바다에 붙인 이름의 꼴인 「게네자렛」은 우리 영어 성경 흠정역에 나오지 않는다. 자리와 넓이. 이 바다는 예루살렘 북동쪽 육십 마일, 지중해 동쪽 이십칠 마일에 있다. 그 꼴은 고르지 않은 타원 곧 배 모양이요 넓은 끝이 북쪽을 향한다. 그 길이가 윌슨에 따르면 십이 마일 반이요 베데커에 따르면 십육 마일 반이며, 너비는 사 마일에서 칠 마일 반이다. 그 물 높이가 철마다 달라 지중해보다 육백에서 칠백 피트 낮고 그 낮음의 평균이 육백이십육 피트쯤이며, 깊이는 백육십 피트이다. 자연의 모습. 이 호수는 거의 끊이지 않는 언덕의 벽에 둘렸고, 디베랴와 게네사렛 벌판과 요단에서 이따금 끊기거나 물러난다. 언덕은 석회암과 현무암과 화산암이요, 화산 활동의 자취가 요단 갈라진 골에도 남달리 넉넉하나 윌슨은 이 호수가 화산에서 생겼음을 가리키는 것을 보지 못한다. 온천이 넉넉하고 지진이 잦다. 요단이 이 호수를 지나며 그 물을 일 마일쯤 물들인다. 호수 물이 얼마쯤 짜나 사람들이 마신다. 물고기가 넉넉하여 여러 종이 발견되었다. 트리스트럼이 말하기를 「그 떼가 몇백 야드 길이의 놀라운 검은 덩이요, 검은 지느러미가 더 빽빽할 수 없을 만큼 물 밖으로 내밀었다. 그런 떼를 가둔 그물이 찢어지는 것이 이상하지 않다. 그러나 물이 그렇게 우글거릴 수 있으리라 믿지 못하였을 만큼 이 호수에 물고기가 우글거리는데도, 나룻배 말고는 그 온 넓이에 배가 둘뿐이다」 한다(『이스라엘 땅』 430쪽). 베데커는 초라한 고깃배 셋을 짚는다. 우리 구주께서 갈릴리 바다에서 보신 수많은 배를 나그네에게 일깨우는 것이 이것뿐이다. 요세푸스가 그 물 위에서 유대인과 베스파시아누스의 군사 사이에 있었던 배 싸움을 그린다. 사납고 홀연한 폭풍이 우리 주의 때에 그러하였듯 오늘도 이 호수에 흔하다. 성경의 역사. 이 호수가 구약에 드물게, 그것도 오히려 곁들여 언급된다(민수기 34:11; 신명기 3:17; 여호수아 11:2; 역대상 12:3; 열왕기상 15:20). 그 으뜸 관심은 우리 구주의 공적인 사역과 이어진 데에 있다. 그 기슭에 「본 동네」가 있었고(마태복음 9:1), 갈릴리의 고깃배에서 그가 시몬 베드로와 그 형제 안드레와 그 동무 야고보와 요한을 부르시어 그때부터 「사람을 취하게」 하셨으며(마태복음 4:18,22; 마가복음 1:16-20; 누가복음 5:1-11), 그 위에서 풍랑을 잔잔하게 하시고 바람과 바다가 그에게 순종하게 하셨다(마태복음 8:23-27; 마태복음 14:22-33; 마태복음 17:27과 마가복음 7:31-35도 보라). 디베랴 바다에서 그리스도께서 부활 뒤에 제자들에게 나타나셨다(요한복음 21장). 그 기슭에 섰던 아홉 넘는 인구 많은 성 가운데 더 중요한 것은 벳새다와 가버나움과 고라신과 디베랴와 막달라였다. 오늘의 모습. 포터가 저녁에 아름다운 자리의 제 장막 문에서 본 이 호수를 아름답게 그린다. 「고요가 깊었다. 자연조차 잠든 듯하였다. 강이 소리 없이 흘러갔고 바다가 닦은 거울처럼 앞에 펼쳐졌다. … 호수 동쪽에 바산의 높은 대지의 옆이 산줄기처럼 솟았고, 그 북쪽 끝에서 내 눈이 몇천이 먹은 저 긍휼의 이적의 바로 그 자리에 머물렀으며, 그 남쪽 끝에서 「돼지 떼가 다 비탈로 내리달아 바다에서 몰사한」 심판의 이적의 자리에 머물렀다. 서쪽 멀리 디베랴의 부서진 성벽이 호수의 품에서 솟는 듯하였고, 그 뒤에 어두운 산이 있어 그 굴진 벼랑에 배운 랍비 여럿의 재가 쉬며, 그 온 위로 다볼의 우아한 둥근 꼭대기가 나타났다. 더 오른쪽 흰 모래톱에 막달라의 오두막이 보였고, 게네사렛 해안이 거기서 북쪽으로 그리스도의 본 동네 가버나움까지 뻗었다.」 오늘 이 호수는 거의 아주 버려져 고깃배 서넛만 있을 뿐이다. 그리스도 때에는 돛단배로 덮였고, 둘린 서쪽 기슭인 게네사렛 벌판은 요세푸스의 빛나는 그림대로 아름다움과 기름짐의 낙원이었다. 콘더 부자가 이 이름난 바다를 배 모양이요 크기가 영국 윈더미어 호수와 비슷하다 그린다. 그들이 더하기를 「북쪽 말고는 석회암 벼랑에 둘렸으니, 북쪽에서는 비스듬한 비탈이 위 갈릴리의 가장 높은 산줄기 밑동에서 뻗은 현무암 대지에서 기슭으로 이끈다. 이 호수의 경치는 헐벗었고 사해의 것보다 훨씬 밋밋하다. 물가가 좁으나 북서쪽에서는 벼랑이 물러나 기름진 벌판(게네사렛)을 남기니 길이 이 마일 반에 너비 일 마일이요 여러 좋은 샘이 적신다. 북쪽의 자갈 깔린 트인 기슭이 여러 만으로 나뉘고 짙은 협죽도 덤불이 둘렸다. 남동쪽에 종려 숲이 있고 서쪽 기슭에 종려가 몇 그루 흩어져 있다. 서쪽의 붉은 벼랑과 동쪽의 가파른 비탈은 헐벗고 쓸쓸하나, 잔잔한 날씨에 둘린 언덕을 비추고 햇빛에 빛나는 이 호수의 단물이 아름다운 경치를 이루니 저녁에 더욱 그러하다. 이 바다는 물고기 떼와 홀연한 우레 폭풍의 사나움과 그 기슭의 온천으로 남다르다. 이 호수 언저리는 또한 남달리 화산의 흔들림을 받기 쉽다.」(『성경 편람』 215쪽, 1879년.) 매닝 목사가 이 호수에서 홀연하고 사나운 폭풍을 만났으니, 신약 역사의 여러 자세한 것을 밝혀 준다. 「밝고 구름 없는 아침에 나는 동쪽 기슭과 요단이 호수로 드는 지점을 살피려 배를 탔다. 물에 잔물결 하나 없었고 바람도 느낄 수 없었다. 거의 알림도 없이 바람이 일었다. 거품을 인 물결이 뱃전을 넘기 시작하였다. 나는 평평하고 높인 고물의 방석 곧 「베개」 위에 「배 뒷부분에」 앉아 뱃사람들이 「힘겹게 노 젓는」 것을 보았다. 그러나 그 온 애씀이 헛되었다. 「바람이 거슬렀으므로」 나아갈 수 없었다. 마침내 하나가 물에 뛰어들어 얼마쯤 헤엄치고 얼마쯤 걸어서 배를 기슭으로 끌었다.」(『거룩한 들』 205쪽.) 윌슨 대위도 비슷한 홀연한 폭풍을 겪었다.

「※ 원문 오류: 「1 Mace. 11:67」의 「Mace.」는 「Macc.」의 글자가 깨진 것이다. 이 사전에서 마카베오서를 드는 자리마다 되풀이되는 깨짐으로, 글자층을 만들 때 한꺼번에 생긴 것이다. 한글은 마카베오상으로 옮겼다.」

variants.definition: GAL'ILEE (circle, circuit), a name in the O.T. for a small district in the northern mountains of Naphtali, around Kedesh-naphtali, and including 20 towns given by Solomon to Hiram, king of Tyre, Josh 20:7 ,Josh 21:32; 1 Kgs 9:11; 2 Kgs 15:29, and called "Galilee of the nations" in Isa 9:1. Devastated during the wars of the Captivity, it was repeopled by strangers. In the time of the Maccabees they probably outnumbered the Jewish population, and gave their new name to a much wider district. In the time of our Lord, Palestine was divided into three provinces, of which Galilee was the most northern. It included the whole region from the Plain of Jezreel to the Litany (Leontes) River, being about 50 miles long by 20 to 25 miles wide. The northern part was known as Upper and the southern part as Lower Galilee. These included the territories given to Asher, Naphtali, Zebulun, and Issachar. The country was famed for its fertility, rich pastures, and fine forests. The portion west of the lake was the most beautiful. In the Roman period the population was dense, Josephus estimating it at 2,000,000 or 3,000,000, though that is probably an exaggeration. It had a mixed population of heathens, foreigners, and Jews. The latter, having a strong, if not dominant, influence, were less strict and less acquainted with the Law than their southern Judaean neighbors, by whom they were little esteemed. The noted mountains of Galilee were Carmel, Gilboa, and Tabor; the towns were Nazareth, Cana, Tiberias, Chorazin, Bethsaida, and Capernaum. Jesus spent the greater portion of his life and ministry in Galilee. Many of his most remarkable miracles, teachings, and labors were within this province of Galilee. His disciples were chiefly from this region. Acts 1:11. After the fall of Jerusalem, Galilee became the residence of celebrated rabbis and the centre of Jewish schools of learning.
variants.definition_ko: '둘레', '지경'이라는 뜻으로, 구약에서는 납달리 북쪽 산지의 게데스납달리 일대 작은 지역의 이름이며, 솔로몬이 두로 왕 히람에게 준 스무 성읍을 포함했다(수 20:7, 왕상 9:11). 사 9:1에서는 '이방의 갈릴리'라 불린다. 포로기 전쟁 중 황폐해진 후 이방인이 다시 들어와 살았고, 마카베오 시대에는 이들이 유대인 인구를 넘어섰을 것이며 그 새 이름이 훨씬 넓은 지역에 붙었다. 주님 당시 팔레스타인은 세 지방으로 나뉘었고 갈릴리가 가장 북쪽이었다. 이스르엘 평야에서 리타니 강까지 길이 약 50마일, 너비 20~25마일이었다. 북부는 상갈릴리, 남부는 하갈릴리라 불렸으며 아셀, 납달리, 스불론, 잇사갈에 준 땅을 포함했다. 비옥함과 풍성한 초장, 좋은 숲으로 유명했다.

variants.definition: GALILEE, SEA OF, a small lake of deep interest to the Bible-reader as the scene of some of the most remarkable works of Jesus. The lake is named from the district or province of Galilee. It was known by several other names, as the sea of Chinnereth, Num 34:11; Deut 3:17, or Chinneroth. Josh 11:2; 1 Chr 12:3, or Cinneroth, 1 Kgs 15:20, probably from a town of that name which stood on its shore. Josh 19:35; the lake of Gennesaret, Luke 5:1, from the plain or land of that name on its north-western side. Matt 14:34; Mark 6:53; the sea of Tiberias, from the celebrated city of that name, John 6:1; and the sea, Matt 4:15. It is also called Gennesar in the Apocryjphal book of Maccabees, 1 Mace. 11:67. Its present name is Bahr Tabariyeh. It is worthy of note that all the towns whose names were applied to this lake were situated upon its western side. "Gennezareth," which is a form of the name also given to the sea by many authors, is not found in the A.V. of our English Bible. Situation and Extent. — This sea is 60 miles north-east from Jerusalem, and 27 east of the Mediterranean Sea. Its form is an irregular oval or pear-shape, the broad end being toward the north. Its length is 12 1/2 miles according to Wilson, 16 1/2 according to Baedeker, and its breadth from 4 to 7 1/2 miles. Its level varies at different seasons, and is from 600 to 700 feet below the Mediterranean, the mean depression being about 626 feet, and its depth 160 feet. Physical Features. — The lake is surrounded by an almost continuous wall of hills, broken or receding occasionally, as at Tiberias, the plain of Gennesaret, and at the Jordan. The hills are of limestone, basalt, and volcanic rocks, indications of volcanic action being also specially abundant in the Jordanic chasm, though Wilson sees nothing to indicate a volcanic origin of the lake. Hot springs abound; earthquakes are frequent. The Jordan runs through the lake, coloring its water for a mile. The water of the lake is slightly salty, but drunk by the people. Fish abound, many species having been found. Tristram says: "The shoals were marvellous black masses of many hundred yards long, with the black fins projecting out of the water as thickly as they could pack. No wonder that any net should break which enclosed such a shoal! Yet though the lake swarms with fish as I could not have believed water could swarm, there are but two boats existing on its whole extent besides a ferry-boat." (Land of Israel, p. 430.) Baedeker notes three miserable fishing-boats. These are all that are left to remind the traveller of the numerous boats which our Saviour saw on the Sea of Galilee. Josephus describes a naval engagement which took place on its waters between the Jews and the soldiers of Vespasian. Violent and Sketch-Map of the Sea of Galilee. (Palestine Exploration Fund.) sudden storms are common now on the lake, as in our Lord's day. Scripture History. — This lake is mentioned in the O.T. but seldom, and then rather incidentally, as in Num 34:11; Deut 3:17; Josh 11:2; 1 Chr 12:3; 1 Kgs 15:20. Its chief interest is its association with the public ministry of our Saviour. Upon its shores was "his own city," Matt 9:1; from fishing-boats on Galilee he called Simon Peter and his brother Andrew, and his partners James and John, who were thenceforth "to catch men," Matt 4:18,Matt 4:22; Mark 1:16-20; Luke 5:1-11; on it he stilled the tempest and made the winds and the sea obev him. Matt 8:23-27; Matt 14:22-33; see also Matt 17:27; Mark 7:31-35; at the Sea of Tiberias Christ also showed himself to the disciples after his resurrection. John 21. Of the nine or more populous cities which stood upon its shores, the more important were Bethsaida, Capernaum, Chorazin, Tiberias, and Magdala. Present Appearance. — Porter gives an eloquent description of the lake as it appeared to him from his tent-door, on a lovely spot, at evening: " The silence was profound. Even Nature seemed to have fallen asleep. The river glided noiselessly past; the sea was spread before me like a polished mirror. . . . East of the lake the side of Bashan's lofty plateau rose as a mountain-chain, and at its northern end my eye rested on the very scene of that miracle of mercy where thousands were fed, and at its southern end on that of the miracle of judgment, where 'the whole herd of swine ran violently down a steep place, and perished in the waters.' Away to the west the shattered ramparts of Tiberias seemed to rise out of the bosom of the lake, and behind them a dark mountain, in whose caverned cliffs repose the ashes of many a learned rabbin, while over all appeared the graceful rounded top of Tabor. Farther to the right, on the white strand, I saw the huts of Magdala, with the coast of Gennesaret extending from it northward to Capernaum — Christ's own city." At the present time the lake is almost utterly forsaken: only three or four fisher-boats can be found there; while at the time of Christ it was covered with sailing-vessels, and the surrounding western shore (the plain of Gennesaret) was, according to the glowing description of Josephus, a paradise of beauty and fertility. F.R. and C.R. Conder describe the famous sea as pear-shaped, and resembling in size the English lake Windermere. They add: "It is surrounded with precipices of limestone, except on the north, where a shelving slope leads to the shore from a plateau of basalt extending from the foot of the highest range of Upper Galilee. The scenery of the lake is bare, and much tamer The Sea of Galilee from Tiberias. (After original Photograph.) than that of the Dead Sea. The beach is narrow except on the north-west, where the cliffs recede, leaving a fertile plain (Gennesaret), 2 1/2 miles long and 1 mile broad, watered by several fine springs. The pebbly open shore on the north is broken into numerous bays, and is fringed with dark oleander bushes. On the south-eastern side is a palm-grove, and a few palms dot the western shore. The ruddy cliffs on the west and the steep slopes on the east are bare and desolate, but the sweet waters of the lake, in calm weather mirroring the surrounding hills and shining in the sun, present a beautiful scene, especially at evening. The sea is remarkable for its shoals of fish, for the violence of its sudden thunder-storms, and for the hot springs along its shores. The neighborhood of the lake is also peculiarly subject to volcanic disturbances." —Handbook of the Bible, p. 215 (1879). The Rev. Dr. S. Manning encountered a sudden and violent storm on this lake, illustrating many of the details of N.T. history: "I had taken a boat, on a bright, cloudless morning, to explore the eastern shores and the point where the Jordan enters the lake. There was not a ripple on the water, not a perceptible current in the air. Almost without warning, the wind rose: the waves, crested with foam, began to break over the sides of the boat. I was sitting on a cushion, or 'pillow,' on the flat, raised stern, 'in the hinder part of the ship,' and watched the crew 'toiling and rowing.' But all their efforts were in vain. They were unable to make any way, for 'the wind was contrary.' At length one of them jumped overboard, and, partly swimming, partly wading, towed the vessel ashore." —Holy Fields, p. 205. Capt. Wilson experienced a similar sudden storm.
variants.definition_ko: '둘레', '지경'이라는 뜻으로, 구약에서는 납달리 북쪽 산지의 게데스납달리 일대 작은 지역의 이름이며, 솔로몬이 두로 왕 히람에게 준 스무 성읍을 포함했다(수 20:7, 왕상 9:11). 사 9:1에서는 '이방의 갈릴리'라 불린다. 포로기 전쟁 중 황폐해진 후 이방인이 다시 들어와 살았고, 마카베오 시대에는 이들이 유대인 인구를 넘어섰을 것이며 그 새 이름이 훨씬 넓은 지역에 붙었다. 주님 당시 팔레스타인은 세 지방으로 나뉘었고 갈릴리가 가장 북쪽이었다. 이스르엘 평야에서 리타니 강까지 길이 약 50마일, 너비 20~25마일이었다. 북부는 상갈릴리, 남부는 하갈릴리라 불렸으며 아셀, 납달리, 스불론, 잇사갈에 준 땅을 포함했다. 비옥함과 풍성한 초장, 좋은 숲으로 유명했다.

variants.definition: GALILEE, SEA OF, a small lake of deep interest to the Bible-reader as the scene of some of the most remarkable works of Jesus. The lake is named from the district or province of Galilee. It was known by several other names, as the sea of Chinnereth, Num 34:11; Deut 3:17, or Chinneroth. Josh 11:2; 1 Chr 12:3, or Cinneroth, 1 Kgs 15:20, probably from a town of that name which stood on its shore. Josh 19:35; the lake of "Gennezareth," which is a form of the name also given to the sea by many authors, is not found in the A.V. of our English Bible.Gennesaret, Luke 5:1, from the plain or land of that name on its north-western side. Matt 14:34; Mark 6:53; the sea of Tiberias, from the celebrated city of that name, John 6:1; and the sea, Matt 4:15. It is also called Gennesar in the Apocryjphal book of Maccabees, 1 Mace. 11:67. Its present name is Bahr Tabariyeh. It is worthy of note that all the towns whose names were applied to this lake were situated upon its western side. Situation and Extent. — This sea is 60 miles north-east from Jerusalem, and 27 east of the Mediterranean Sea. Its form is an irregular oval or pear-shape, the broad end being toward the north. Its length is 12 1/2 miles according to Wilson, 16 1/2 according to Baedeker, and its breadth from 4 to 7 1/2 miles. Its level varies at different seasons, and is from 600 to 700 feet below the Mediterranean, the mean depression being about 626 feet, and its depth 160 feet. Physical Features. — The lake is surrounded by an almost continuous wall of hills, broken or receding occasionally, as at Tiberias, the plain of Gennesaret, and at the Jordan. The hills are of limestone, basalt, and volcanic rocks, indications of volcanic action being also specially abundant in the Jordanic chasm, though Wilson sees nothing to indicate a volcanic origin of the lake. Hot springs abound; earthquakes are frequent. The Jordan runs through the lake, coloring its water for a mile. The water of the lake is slightly salty, but drunk by the people. Fish abound, many species having been found. Tristram says: "The shoals were marvellous black masses of many hundred yards long, with the black fins projecting out of the water as thickly as they could pack. No wonder that any net should break which enclosed such a shoal! Yet though the lake swarms with fish as I could not have believed water could swarm, there are but two boats existing on its whole extent besides a ferry-boat." (Land of Israel, p. 430.) Baedeker notes three miserable fishing-boats. These are all that are left to remind the traveller of the numerous boats which our Saviour saw on the Sea of Galilee. Josephus describes a naval engagement which took place on its waters between the Jews and the soldiers of Vespasian. Violent and Sketch-Map of the Sea of Galilee. (Palestine Exploration Fund.) sudden storms are common now on the lake, as in our Lord's day. Scripture History. — This lake is mentioned in the O.T. but seldom, and then rather incidentally, as in Num 34:11; Deut 3:17; Josh 11:2; 1 Chr 12:3; 1 Kgs 15:20. Its chief interest is its association with the public ministry of our Saviour. Upon its shores was "his own city," Matt 9:1; from fishing-boats on Galilee he called Simon Peter and his brother Andrew, and his partners James and John, who were thenceforth "to catch men," Matt 4:18,Matt 4:22; Mark 1:16-20; Luke 5:1-11; on it he stilled the tempest and made the winds and the sea obev him. Matt 8:23-27; Matt 14:22-33; see also Matt 17:27; Mark 7:31-35; at the Sea of Tiberias Christ also showed himself to the disciples after his resurrection. John 21. Of the nine or more populous cities which stood upon its shores, the more important were Bethsaida, Capernaum, Chorazin, Tiberias, and Magdala. Present Appearance. — Porter gives an eloquent description of the lake as it appeared to him from his tent-door, on a lovely spot, at evening: " The silence was profound. Even Nature seemed to have fallen asleep. The river glided noiselessly past; the sea was spread before me like a polished mirror. . . . East of the lake the side of Bashan's lofty plateau rose as a mountain-chain, and at its northern end my eye rested on the very scene of that miracle of mercy where thousands were fed, and at its southern end on that of the miracle of judgment, where 'the whole herd of swine ran violently down a steep place, and perished in the waters.' Away to the west the shattered ramparts of Tiberias seemed to rise out of the bosom of the lake, and behind them a dark mountain, in whose caverned cliffs repose the ashes of many a learned rabbin, while over all appeared the graceful rounded top of Tabor. Farther to the right, on the white strand, I saw the huts of Magdala, with the coast of Gennesaret extending from it northward to Capernaum — Christ's own city." At the present time the lake is almost utterly forsaken: only three or four fisher-boats can be found there; while at the time of Christ it was covered with sailing-vessels, and the surrounding western shore (the plain of Gennesaret) was, according to the glowing description of Josephus, a paradise of beauty and fertility. F.R. and C.R. Conder describe the famous sea as pear-shaped, and resembling in size the English lake Windermere. They add: "It is surrounded with precipices of limestone, except on the north, where a shelving slope leads to the shore from a plateau of basalt extending from the foot of the highest range of Upper Galilee. The scenery of the lake is bare, and much tamer The Sea of Galilee from Tiberias. (After original Photograph.) than that of the Dead Sea. The beach is narrow except on the north-west, where the cliffs recede, leaving a fertile plain (Gennesaret), 2 1/2 miles long and 1 mile broad, watered by several fine springs. The pebbly open shore on the north is broken into numerous bays, and is fringed with dark oleander bushes. On the south-eastern side is a palm-grove, and a few palms dot the western shore. The ruddy cliffs on the west and the steep slopes on the east are bare and desolate, but the sweet waters of the lake, in calm weather mirroring the surrounding hills and shining in the sun, present a beautiful scene, especially at evening. The sea is remarkable for its shoals of fish, for the violence of its sudden thunder-storms, and for the hot springs along its shores. The neighborhood of the lake is also peculiarly subject to volcanic disturbances." —Handbook of the Bible, p. 215 (1879). The Rev. Dr. S. Manning encountered a sudden and violent storm on this lake, illustrating many of the details of N.T. history: "I had taken a boat, on a bright, cloudless morning, to explore the eastern shores and the point where the Jordan enters the lake. There was not a ripple on the water, not a perceptible current in the air. Almost without warning, the wind rose: the waves, crested with foam, began to break over the sides of the boat. I was sitting on a cushion, or 'pillow,' on the flat, raised stern, 'in the hinder part of the ship,' and watched the crew 'toiling and rowing.' But all their efforts were in vain. They were unable to make any way, for 'the wind was contrary.' At length one of them jumped overboard, and, partly swimming, partly wading, towed the vessel ashore." —Holy Fields, p. 205. Capt. Wilson experienced a similar sudden storm.
variants.definition_ko: 예수님의 가장 놀라운 일들이 벌어진 무대로 성경 독자에게 깊은 관심의 대상인 작은 호수다. 갈릴리 지방의 이름을 땄다. 긴네렛 바다(민수기 34:11, 신명기 3:17), 긴네롯(여호수아 11:2), 긴네롯(열왕기상 15:20)이라고도 불렸는데, 호숫가에 있던 같은 이름의 성읍에서 온 듯하다(여호수아 19:35). 게네사렛 호수(누가복음 5:1)라고도 하는데 북서쪽의 그 이름의 평야에서 왔고, 그 유명한 성읍의 이름을 딴 디베랴 바다(요한복음 6:1), 그냥 '바다'(마태복음 4:15)라고도 불린다. 지금 이름은 바흐르 타바리예다. 이 호수에 이름을 준 성읍들이 모두 서편에 있었다는 점이 주목할 만하다.

entries.definition: GALL, BILE, an animal fluid, of exceedingly bitter taste, secreted by the liver. Ps 69:21. Allusion is made to it in Job 16:13; Job 20:14, Job 20:25; Lam 2:11, and elsewhere. But by the same word, in Ps 69:21, reference is made to the extraction of a very bitter herb, Deut 29:18; Deut 32:32, perhaps hemlock. Hos 10:4. It was so bitter as to be used as a generic term for bitter substances; as sour wine or sour cider, etc., is called "vinegar." Comp. Matt 27:34; Mark 15:23; Acts 8:23. See Myrrh.
entries.definition_ko: 간에서 분비되는 몹시 쓴 동물의 체액이다(시편 69:21, 욥기 16:13, 20:14,25, 예레미야애가 2:11). 그러나 시편 69:21에서 같은 말이 매우 쓴 풀, 아마도 독당근의 즙을 가리킨다(신명기 29:18:32, 호세아 10:4). 하도 써서 쓴 것들을 두루 가리키는 말로 쓰였으니, 신 포도주나 신 사과주를 '초'라 부르는 것과 같다(마태복음 27:34, 마가복음 15:23, 사도행전 8:23).

동방 가옥에 흔한 툇마루다. 그러나 흠정역의 이 말은 히브리어의 정확한 번역이 아니며, 최근 연구에 따르면 주랑 또는 판벽을 뜻한다(아가 1:17, 에스겔 41:15).

entries.definition: GAL'LIM (heaps), the home of David's wife, 1 Sam 25:44; a village of Benjamin, Isa 10:30; now perhaps Khirbet es-Soma. Conder proposes Beit Jala.

entries.definition: GAL'LIO, proconsul of Achaia and brother of Seneca, the famous philosopher, who describes him as a man of great mildness and simplicity. Acts 18:12. Paul was brought before his tribunal at Corinth by the Jews, who accused him of blasphemy. Acts 18:6. Gallio dismissed the case as one not cognizable by a Roman court. Acts 18:14-15. He deemed the offence at best a trivial one. Like his brother Seneca, Gallio was executed at the command of Nero.
entries.definition_ko: 아가야의 총독이자 유명한 철학자 세네카의 형제로, 세네카는 그를 매우 온화하고 소박한 사람으로 묘사한다(사도행전 18:12). 고린도에서 유대인들이 바울을 신성모독으로 고발하여 그 재판정에 세웠으나, 갈리오는 로마 법정이 다룰 사안이 아니라며 물리쳤다(사도행전 18:14-15). 그 죄목을 기껏해야 사소한 것으로 여긴 것이다. 형제 세네카처럼 네로의 명으로 처형되었다.
